subject: Unit 3 • Union Executive and Parliament
question: Under the Constitution of India, who has the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill, and for how many days at most may the Rajya Sabha hold it?
options: The President of India; up to 14 days
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha; up to 14 days
The Union Finance Minister; up to 30 days
The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs; up to 14 days
explanation: Article 110(3) of the Constitution provides that the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final. Under Article 109, a Money Bill may be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and only on the President's recommendation. After the Lok Sabha passes it, the Rajya Sabha may hold it for no more than 14 days. If it does not return the Bill within that period, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form approved by the Lok Sabha.

subject: Unit 3 • Parliamentary Committees
question: Which of the following standing financial committees of Parliament has 30 members, all of whom are elected exclusively from the Lok Sabha?
explanation: The Estimates Committee, constituted in 1950 following a recommendation associated with John Mathai, is the largest parliamentary financial committee. It has 30 members, all elected annually from the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha has no representation on it. The membership was increased from 25 to 30 in 1956. By contrast, the Public Accounts Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings each have 22 members—15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

subject: Unit 3 • Judiciary: Supreme Court and High Courts
question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India may the President refer a question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its advisory opinion?
explanation: Article 143 empowers the President to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion on a question of law or fact of public importance. A reference under Article 143(1) is ordinarily heard by a Constitution Bench of at least five judges. The opinion is advisory rather than binding on the President. Article 131 concerns the Court's original jurisdiction, Article 137 its power to review its judgments, and Article 142 its power to pass orders necessary to do complete justice.

subject: Unit 3 • Constitutional Bodies: Election Commission and CAG
question: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, who is the third member of the selection committee that recommends appointments, alongside the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha?
options: A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
explanation: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, the selection committee recommending appointments consists of three members: (1) the Prime Minister, who chairs it; (2) the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, or the leader of the largest opposition party where applicable; and (3) a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

subject: Unit 3 • Panchayati Raj and Local Government
question: Which Article, added to Part IX of the Constitution by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, provides for the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats?
explanation: Article 243-I provides for the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission at the end of every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend the distribution of certain taxes between the State and local bodies. Article 243-Y makes related provision for municipalities. Article 243-K concerns State Election Commissions, Article 243-D deals with reservation of seats in Panchayats, and Article 243-G concerns Panchayats' powers and responsibilities, including matters listed in the Eleventh Schedule.

subject: Unit 3 • Public Policy, Good Governance and Right to Information
question: Under Section 7(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, within what period must a Public Information Officer provide requested information when it concerns a person's 'life or liberty'?
explanation: Under Section 7(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, a Public Information Officer ordinarily must respond within 30 days of receiving an application; a request submitted through an Assistant Public Information Officer may have an additional five days. The proviso to Section 7(1), however, requires information concerning the life or liberty of a person to be provided within 48 hours.

subject: Unit 3 • Lokpal and Lokayuktas
question: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, what is the maximum number of members the Lokpal may have in addition to its Chairperson, and what minimum proportion of its members must be Judicial Members?
options: Up to 6 members; at least 33% Judicial Members
Up to 10 members; at least 50% Judicial Members
Up to 8 members; at least 50% Judicial Members
Up to 5 members; at least 50% Judicial Members
explanation: Section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 provides for a Lokpal consisting of a Chairperson and up to eight members. At least 50% of the members must be Judicial Members. The Act also requires at least 50% of the members to be drawn from the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, minorities and women. The Chairperson and members hold office for five years or until they reach 70 years of age, whichever is earlier.

subject: Unit 3 • Rights-Related Issues and Commissions
question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) by inserting Article 338B into the Constitution?
explanation: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes, which had previously been a statutory body under the 1993 Act. It inserted Article 338B and added Article 342A. The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 later restored the States' and Union Territories' power to prepare and maintain their own lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes. Article 338 concerns the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, while Article 338A concerns the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

subject: Unit 3 • International Organisations and the United Nations
question: Which of the six principal organs of the United Nations is headquartered not in New York, United States, but at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands?
explanation: The six principal organs established by the UN Charter are the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council, International Court of Justice and Secretariat. Five are headquartered in New York. The International Court of Justice is based at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands, and consists of 15 judges elected by the General Assembly and Security Council for nine-year terms.
